messages.author: ff9e47f6a1af1908
messages.subject: Likelihood function marginalized in multilevel IRT model
parts:
Hello everybody,

I'm having a problem that I do not know how to solve via Stan. I'm working with a multilevel IRT polytomous model and I do not know how to calculate the marginalized likelihood, which is described in Fox's (2010) book:







In this case, theta depends on beta, which depends on gamma (hierarchical structure).

If there were this hierarchical structure, I think it would be easy. Look at the code for the non-multilevel case:

generated quantities {
  real dev;
  vector[J] log_lik[N];
  dev <- 0;
  for (i in 1:N) {
    for (j in 1:J) {
      log_lik[i, j] <- categorical_log(Y[i, j], prob[i, j, 1:m]);
      dev <- dev + (-2) * log_lik[i, j];
    }
  }
}

But, and for marginalized likelihood (as the equation presented)?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Likelihood function marginalized in multilevel IRT model
parts:
There's no way to compute integrals for marginal likelihoods
numerically in Stan (though we are working on some underlying tools
for that in the context of max marginal likelihood calcs like lme4
uses).

What we tend to do is not bother with posterior marginal likelihoods
and instead deal directly in posterior predictive inferences, where
the marginalizations become trivial and you get distributions over
any quantities of interest.

But if you want to compute Bayesian alternatives to DIC, such
as WAIC, then you really do need those marginal likelihoods. I don't
know what they do in those cases, but you may want to call this out
in a separate message to the list highlighting the fact that you
want to do model comparison with a model that has latent parameters.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Likelihood function marginalized in multilevel IRT model
parts:
You really need help from Aki, Jonah, or Andrew.

If you write another message that says model comparison,
they'll see it and hopefully help out.

I was suggesting things you can compute without normalization.
You can draw y-predicted from the posterior predictive
p(y-predicted | y) and use those to evaluate event probabilities such
as Pr[y_predict in (a, b) | y]. These can be used to test calibration
and sharpness of the model, for example.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Likelihood function marginalized in multilevel IRT model
parts:
Let me try to reformulate.

Suppose you have observations y, parameters theta, and a latent parameter
z[i] for each observation y[i]. How do you compute the likelihood
p(y | theta)? Stan lets you draw from the posterior p(theta | y). Then
how do you calculate the likelihood p(y | theta). Sure, we know

p(y | theta) = p(y, z | theta) / p(z | theta).

but that just requires us to compute p(z | theta), which I think is
the integral in question here.

I still think Aki and Andrew are the one's the one to ask about
this!

- Bob
